title: Password login, Google linking and admin user management
description:
User request (2026-11-20, verbatim): "add a login with user and password, add basic user management to admin as well to allow user CRUD, need to integrate with google if user that first loged with email try to login with google later, is basic email login ... we will not have recover password, send email no, in admin i can change people password only and give to people a tmp password they must change on login".

This epic holds the design. Subtasks implement it: API + contracts, client, admin SPA. Where the code forces a different shape, keep the BEHAVIOUR below and record the deviation in a tk note.

## Context (read before designing)
- Sessions are stateless HS256 JWTs, sub = e-mail, optional `idp` claim (api/src/user/auth.ts, authz.ts, session-cookie.ts). Web holds an httpOnly cookie on .syscd.live; native sends the token as Bearer.
- `requireUser` and several pre-gate callers resolve the user with `resolveOrCreateSessionUser(email)`, which CREATES a row on first sight. `isAllowed(email, idp)` (user/config.ts) is the per-request allow check; Google sign-in is gated by AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS (`googleAllowed`).
- The Postgres database is SHARED with the running syscd-app: migrations are additive only, `public.users` is shared. Put everything new in NEW tables.
- docs/decisions.md sections "Access sign-in" and "Multi-user" explain the existing rules.

## Identity model
- One user row per e-mail (unchanged). A password is an extra credential on that row, stored in a new table (suggested `user_passwords`: user_id PK FK, password_hash, must_change, temp_expires_at, changed_at, sessions_valid_after).
- "Admin-managed" = the user has a password row. Only an admin creates one (creating a user, or resetting a password of any existing user, including one who so far used Google or Access). No self sign-up, no password recovery, no e-mail sending.
- Password sessions carry idp `password`. They are valid only while: password login is on, the user row exists and is active, a password row exists, and the token's iat >= sessions_valid_after. A password session must NEVER create a user row.
- Google linking: an admin-managed, active user may sign in with Google using the same e-mail even when it is not on AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS (both the web callback and the native /auth/token; Google `email_verified` stays mandatory). It resolves to the SAME user row (google_sub is back-filled as today; a row holding a different google_sub is refused as today). That Google session must also pass the per-request check without being on the env list. The reverse also holds: a Google/Access user given a password by an admin signs in with it into the same row.

## Password rules
- Hash with Bun.password (argon2id). Never log or return a hash or a password; never store a temp password in clear.
- User-chosen passwords: 12 to 128 characters, no composition rules, not equal to the e-mail, not equal to the current/temp password, rejected if in a small built-in list of very common passwords.
- Temp passwords are generated by the SERVER (>= 80 bits of entropy, easy to read out loud and type), returned exactly once in the admin response, expire after 7 days, and force a change.

## Endpoints (contracts in shared/src/contracts/user, zod input AND output)
- POST /auth/password/login {email, password} (pre-gate, JSON only):
  - success: web gets the session cookie and NO token in the body; native asks for a token explicitly and gets {token, email} with no cookie (follow how /auth/exchange returns it).
  - temp password (must_change): NO session. Returns a short-lived (about 10 min) single-purpose change token; POST /auth/password/complete {change_token, new_password} sets the new password, clears must_change and then signs in as above. That token must not be accepted anywhere else (not as a session, not as an OAuth token).
  - every failure that an attacker could use to tell accounts apart (unknown e-mail, no password row, wrong password, disabled user) is the same 401 `invalid_credentials` with comparable timing (verify against a dummy hash when there is nothing to check). An expired temp password may say so (`temp_password_expired`) only after the temp password itself was correct.
  - throttling: failed attempts are counted per normalised e-mail in a new table, for unknown e-mails too, so lockout cannot be used to enumerate. After 5 consecutive failures the e-mail is locked with a growing delay (1 min doubling to a 15 min cap); locked = 429 `too_many_attempts` + Retry-After, checked BEFORE verifying. Success and admin reset clear it. Prune old rows. Add a simple per-IP limiter too (CF-Connecting-IP when present).
  - refuse requests whose Origin header is present and is not one of the allowed app/admin origins.
- POST /auth/password/change {current_password, new_password}: signed-in first-party session only (no OAuth access token, no service token); re-verifies the current password under the same throttle; invalidates the user's other password sessions (sessions_valid_after) and re-issues the caller's.
- GET /auth/providers gains `password: boolean`. /me gains `has_password: boolean`.
- Config: password login is on by default when auth is on; env AUTH_PASSWORD_LOGIN=0 turns the routes into 404 and existing password sessions invalid.
- Admin (requireAdmin; first-party session only; expose api only, not cli/mcp), under /admin/users:
  - GET list: id, email, name, role, status, has_password, must_change_password, temp_expires_at, locked_until, has_google, signed_in_at, last_seen_at, created_at.
  - POST create {email, name?, role?}: new user + temp password, returns the user and `temp_password` once. Existing e-mail = 409.
  - PATCH :id {name?, role?, status?}. E-mail is not editable (it is the session and join key).
  - POST :id/reset-password: new temp password (returned once), must_change, 7-day expiry, clears the throttle, invalidates that user's password sessions. This is the ONLY way an admin changes a password; an admin never types one.
  - DELETE :id: hard delete only when nothing references the user (see `userReferenceColumns` in user/store.ts); otherwise 409 `user_has_data` and the admin disables instead.
  - Guards: an admin cannot disable, demote or delete themself, and the last active admin cannot be disabled, demoted or deleted. Synthetic rows (service user, dev user) are not manageable.
  - Log each admin action (who, what, target) without secrets.
- Disabling a user already blocks every session (existing status check); keep that true for the new paths.

## Out of scope
Password recovery, e-mail sending, self sign-up, MFA, changing an e-mail, users setting a first password themselves.
